title: Discrete packet-plan Mirror latent
hypothesis: A compact discrete packet-plan code can condition one shared packet decoder and improve joint future-mode coverage at lower serialized state than storing one decoder/model per mode, while matching a VQ latent and continuous latent at equal bits.
mirror_coordinate: discrete codebook index selecting a packet plan
task: Synthetic four-step binary packet prediction with correlated modes; learn the conditional joint packet distribution from support examples and evaluate joint NLL, valid-packet mass, mode coverage and bytes.

development.selection_metric: Freeze decoder family and codebook size using dev joint NLL; code budget fixed at 2 bits/packet.

fresh.split: Each fresh world generates new mode mixtures and packet frequencies; 4096 support packets and 4096 heldout packets. No audit frequency data used in codebook fitting.

success_gate: On >=2/3 fresh worlds, discrete Mirror joint NLL improves by >=0.05 nats/packet over unconditional shared decoder, valid-packet mass >=0.99, and total payload <=60% of independent per-mode model bank. It must also be competitive with same-bit VQ and continuous latent controls to support Mirror-specific value.
failure_gate: FAIL if the improvement or validity gate fails on >=2/3 worlds, if the payload exceeds 60% of independent mode models without a quality advantage, or if a same-bit native latent control matches or beats Mirror on quality/bytes.
boundaries: does not establish PTP performance on language models
2-bit logical code does not imply independent capacity without measured heldout joint quality
small codebooks and decoder intentionally kept tiny for CPU screening
